Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Comments: Follow up inspection of the Kovalish 3 well conducted on 6/21/2023. Arrived on location at 12:21. Well is not in, or equipped for, production. Onsite equipment consists of wellhead, pumpjack, and electric service box. All equipment is inside bushes/briars/trees to the point of being inaccessible. Review found that Annual Production Reports are current, with last production shown in 2016. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 5/20/2022. Violations were issued on 4/27/2023 for: OGA3211(G) - No well tag or other form of identification of permit number. OGA3211(H) - No Operator ID or signage containing required operator info. OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to report annual integrity monitoring of the well while under Inactive Status. 78.104 - Failure to meet terms of Inactive Status. 78.88 - Failure to report Mechanical Integrity of the well after expiration of Inactive Status. This 6/21/2023 follow up inspection found that none of the above violations have been addressed and all remain outstanding. Response was received from the operator on 5/30/2023 (attached as file) which indicated correct signage/ tag would be installed and the well will be plugged. The Department requests a response to this report with an anticipated timeframe for plugging.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/27/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8236096
Permit API: 129-26521
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: On May 27, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3972746 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3972746, excavation and remediation work had started onsite but did not yet appear to be complete. Two covered excavation stockpile was observed onsite, however the impacted area appeared to remain adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.On the day of this inspection prior to arriving onsite, the Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs who explained that all material that was impacted by the 4/24/2025 crude oil and brine release has been excavated and awaits transport from site. Subsequent backfill and seeding of the formerly impacted area and screening underneath the brine tank location in response to observations made in Photos 9 and 10 of IR 3967072 are to follow.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 3). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 4). The covered excavation stockpiles that were observed onsite during the time IR 3972746 remain (see photos 5, 6, and 10). properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/06/2023 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/06/2023
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 990921
Permit API: 015-23733
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/06/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/6/2023 at 1430 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Blackhill. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371191 is tied to this release within CTS. On 4/6/2023 at ~1300 hours an initial estimate of 4 barrels of produced water was discovered by Blackhill Energy to have been released from the produced water offload area at the Jackson pad. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. I field measured fluids in the rock-lined conveyance channel along the entirety of the southern edge of the pad. All fluids in the rock-lined channel up to the stormwater control basin were field measured at >19.99mS/cm. Fluid flowing in the rock-lined channel was observed entering the stormwater control basin. I collected a sample (0983-377) for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid located in the rock-lined conveyance channel just before entering the stormwater control basin (photo #11). This fluid was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photo #10). Two sumps were constructed along the rock-lined channel to begin collecting any fluids flowing in the channel. The DEP requested that the now impacted stormwater contained in the stormwater basin be collected as a regulated substance due to the release impacting it. As I departed a crew were working on excavating the impacted pad material near the point of release and recovering the fluids that were on the surface of the pad. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Based on the reported release of produced water outside of containment and the discovery of the release entering conveyance channels and reaching the stormwater controls, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23733: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.401Violations of the following, cited against API #015-23733 on 1/3/2023 regarding a separate release remain outstanding at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to Pennfield Energy's 8/17/2021 notification of a crude oil discharge from a stock tank located at the Milford South tank battery, which is located adjacent to this well site. Per Matt Duckett (field representative for Pennfield Energy) the oil/water separator that serves this tank battery failed and resulted in all production fluids entering the stock tank, which did not have the capacity to hold all of the fluid. Crude oil then discharged from an open vent on top of one of the stock tanks and onto the ground within an earthen containment that surrounds all of the tanks at the Milford South tank battery. The estimated quantity of crude oil that was released has been revised after conducting remediation work. Matt Duckett stated that approximately five barrels of crude is a more accurate quantity of product actually released as a result of this incident. Additional details regarding the release can be found in the 'Remarks/Violations' section of this report. This well is equipped for production with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack's electric box.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC

Violation Date: 5/03/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 993565
Permit API: 047-25052
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/03/2023
Comments: This is a complaint inspection following a report by the operator of a large production water spill at this site on 4/26 at 7:30 am. An initial site visit was performed by WQSS Rob Bechtel. This inspection was performed with Seneca's Jeff Passerello.The initial spill occurred when a cast iron gate valve failed as the operator was pumping production water to a stimulation operation on the E09-U pad. The pump was in operation at 50 barrels per minute. The operator was able to stop the leak eventually. Water spread out across the northern edge of the site, entering a perimeter ditch. It then ran around the edge ditch of the site and eventually entered an infiltration berm on the southwest corner of the location. The operator brought in a pump and was able to collect a significant amount of liquid from this location. The operator's estimate is that 1500+ barrels of produced water was released. The operator has scraped up ~150 tons of material from the surface of the location and staged it on site to remove to the landfill. A pump is placed and the operator is using it to pump water collecting in the berm into tanks on site. Water does not appear to have passed the berm at this time, at least superficially. The operator has brought in ARM Group to do an initial analysis of the site and to take samples for removal to the landfill. Further inspection on this site will be done as necessary as cleanup continues.

The GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release occurred on 1/20/2026. He stated the release occurred from a hose failure on a portable heater onsite. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 10 gallons of glycol onto the graveled well pad.Mr. Miller stated remediation had been completed and all impacted gravel/material had been removed and placed into drums. The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 15 foot by 30 foot area adjacent to the portbale heater near the GPUs. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the release/remediation with readings of 0.04mS, 0.03mS, 0.06ms, and 0.04mS being obtained. These readings appeared comparable to the background reading of 0.03mS.Based on observations from this inspection and information provided by the operator, it appears that the spill has been remediated in accordance with current regulations. The Department requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Violations are being issued as immediately corrected.

Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill that was found the morning of 7/31/2020. Per the operator, a leak of brine occurred from a poly tank or the line leading from the separator to the tank and leaked into containment. It then ran around a freshwater drain pipe that was placed in at construction.The well is an open flowing well that appears to in production, with the valves opened. The well is plumbed to a gas separator and a 50 barrel poly tank within containment. Some stained soil is apparent between the separator and the containment, with elevated conductivity >1mS noted using a Soil EC meter probe. Vegetation within the containment is distressed or dead, indicating brine discharge. Down slope from the containment, vegetation has been killed in a band consistent with discharge from or around the freshwater drain. Conductivity measured ~11 mS near the drain and diminished down slope, with the final reading over 1 mS noted approximately 100 feet from the tank, in a scour location that was likely from a stormwater event. The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/27/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/27/2026
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8272212
Permit API: 123-47186
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: This conventional well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There are no surface concerns evident on the well site at this time. 2025 APR and MIA information were submitted for this well.The tank battery for Trinity Mineral Partners' Roell lease is located approximately 500 feet to the west of this well, and is accessed off of Rounds Hill Road.This tank battery consists of two earthen containments. One containment consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks and separators, there are no surface issues evident at this containment. A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/29/2023 to INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC in Gamble Township, Lycoming county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/29/2023
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8166668
Permit API: 081-21757
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Gamble Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/29/2023
Comments: On November 29, 2023, DEP representatives Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted a incident inspection at the Inflection Energy Reynolds Well Pad. Gregg Saunders with Inflection Energy reported on November 28, 2023 that a spill from a separator onsite occurred misting production fluid onto the well pad surface. A valve body on the separator failed and spilled approximately 10 gallons of production fluid onto the well pad surface. Penn E and R was onsite for Inflection and delineated the area of impact. Inflection contractors were using a high vacuum truck to remove some of the impacted area and excavating the remainder of the area where the vacuum truck was not able to handle. The area of impact was about 30 feet by 10 feet. The depth of the excavation ranged from an inch to a foot. Excavation of the area of impact was not complete by the time DEP left the site. Soil conductivity was screened with a soil conductivity meter and ranged from 200 uS/cm to an over range reading on the meter. The upper conductivity limit of the DEP soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The lower range measurement was from an area that the impacted soil had been removed.The spill of production fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management 301.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 918445
Permit API: 117-20691
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/25/2021
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the Seneca Resources - Kinnan Unit 845 in response to report of a release by Joe Hartleb of National Fuel Gas notified the DEP of a release of "5+ gallons of triethylene glycol from a packing column" on the Kinnan Well Site on 5/21/2021 @0930 hours. The weather was 72 degrees, partly cloudy, winds SW @8mph. The spill notification stated Miller Environmental cleaned up the standing glycol and secured the site for the weekend. As of today's inspection Miller Environmental Group was present onsite initiating remediation of the release. Onsite personnel stated they believe the removal of the impacted pad material will involve the stained area, approximately 4' x 6', directly around the stack of the dehydration unit. The equipment and containment will also be washed off and the fluid removed. A lined roll-off waste container was staged onsite and equipment was standing by to begin scraping pad material. Personnel onsite stated they were waiting on personnel from NFG to begin the remediation. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a(b) Mr. Brandon Coldren, Miller Environmental Cleanup, stated due to the estimated volume of less than 1 barrel they planned to visually remediate impacted soils and provide documentation to the Department of disposal. I departed the site at 1015 hours.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8226208
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/20/2025
Comments: On March 20, 2025, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Kriebel Natural Gas Co's RWS Development 001 Well located in Manor Borough, Westmoreland County in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Accompanying on today's inspection was Kriebel representative's Ben Dickun and Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Dickun and Mr. Seich stated that the production tank on site had been emptied prior to our arrival on site and that they were going to install booms in the ditch that runs adjacent to the well site and terminates at a nearby stream downslope. The DEP inquired whether any other remediation efforts were going to be conducted while the DEP was on site or after the inspection, and Mr. Dickun stated that they were awaiting instruction from the DEP. At the time of this inspection, the DEP verbally recommended Kriebel promptly remediate the brine release in accordance with Act 2 protocol. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.During IR 3941481 and 3941519, the DEP collected several soil conductivity readings around the well site to determine the extent of the release and concluded that the brine release was contained to a ditch that runs alongside the well site edge and terminates just before a stream. No elevated conductivity readings were collected in the stream, therefore at the time of that inspection, it did not appear that there were any impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).At the time of this inspection, the DEP took a background soil conductivity upslope and away from the incident area (0.0833 mS), and then soil conductivity readings were taken within the ditch: Right by the production equipment (1.225 mS and 1.105 mS), right by a inlet that appeared to be plugged with rocks and plastic (1.165 mS), right by an outlet that appeared to be dry at the time of this inspection (0.828 mS), and then in the ditch leading up to where it terminates just before the stream (1.132 mS, 1.236 mS, and 1.348 mS,). Readings taken directly upslope of the ditch on both sides were comparable to the background reading, while readings taken inside the ditch were elevated, subjugating that the release still appears to be contained to the ditch. To determine whether the stream had become impacted from the brine release, at the time of this inspection, a soil conductivity readings was taken on the stream bank directly downslope of where the ditch terminates (0.593 mS), then a soil (0.402 mS) and fluid (0.459 mS) conductivity reading was taken in the stream directly downslope of where the ditch terminates and lastly, a fluid reading was taken upslope (0.527 mS) and downslope (0.524 mS) of this area. Based on the DEP's observations and these conductivity readings, it appears that the WOC at the time of this inspection remain unscathed from the brine release. The DEP recommends immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

No elevated conductivity readings were collected in the stream, therefore at the time of that inspection, it did not appear that there were any impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).At the time of this inspection, the DEP took a background soil conductivity upslope and away from the incident area (0.0833 mS), and then soil conductivity readings were taken within the ditch: Right by the production equipment (1.225 mS and 1.105 mS), right by a inlet that appeared to be plugged with rocks and plastic (1.165 mS), right by an outlet that appeared to be dry at the time of this inspection (0.828 mS), and then in the ditch leading up to where it terminates just before the stream (1.132 mS, 1.236 mS, and 1.348 mS,). Readings taken directly upslope of the ditch on both sides were comparable to the background reading, while readings taken inside the ditch were elevated, subjugating that the release still appears to be contained to the ditch. To determine whether the stream had become impacted from the brine release, at the time of this inspection, a soil conductivity readings was taken on the stream bank directly downslope of where the ditch terminates (0.593 mS), then a soil (0.402 mS) and fluid (0.459 mS) conductivity reading was taken in the stream directly downslope of where the ditch terminates and lastly, a fluid reading was taken upslope (0.527 mS) and downslope (0.524 mS) of this area. Based on the DEP's observations and these conductivity readings, it appears that the WOC at the time of this inspection remain unscathed from the brine release. The DEP recommends immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/15/2025 to TITUS ENERGY LLC in Monroe Township, Clarion county. 78.89(e) - OPERATING WELLS - GAS MIGRATION RESPONSE - Operator failed to take additional actions as required by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TITUS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2025
Violation Code: 78.89(e) - OPERATING WELLS - GAS MIGRATION RESPONSE - Operator failed to take additional actions as required by the Department.
Violation ID: 8233560
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing investigation into stray gas migration, involving combustible gas detected at the foundation of a nearby private residence. The well is situated approximately 650 feet north-northwest of the complainant’s residence. During the inspection, an updated well record was reviewed. The well was actively producing via the 4-inch production string, with valves on the 7-inch intermediate casing and the 4-inch production string annuls closed at the time of inspection Bubbling was observed in the annular space between the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing. Combustible gas screening using a calibrated gas meter indicated a concentration of 29% LEL (1.4%) in this annulus. According to the well records, both the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing were cemented to surface. The presence of combustible gas in the annulus suggests potential defects in the casing and/or cement integrity. Additionally, no check valve was observed on the production lines exiting the well. To further assess possible migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the wellhead in the cardinal directions, each about 3 feet deep. No detectable levels of combustible gas were found in the slam bar holes at the time of the inspection. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on 05/15/2025 was used for combustible gas screening during the inspection. It is noted that the operator has not responded to or completed the recommended corrective actions outlined in Inspection ID# 3913271. These actions were communicated via certified mail (USPS# 9589 0710 5270 1975 0616 42), sent on 02/13/2025 and received by the operator on 02/19/2025. As a result, the violations identified during this inspection are now being formally imposed on this well.
